request.spec: Exports taken while a preview date is set use the preview figures.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Exports taken while a preview date is set use the preview figures.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The app already does what this change asks, so I didn't change any code. I ran `bin/e2e` before touching anything and all 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` passed: the main "preview exports" test and its three scenarios.

Both exports already use the preview date:
- **Reading the data:** while a preview date is set, every read of a sheet's records gets `?preview=<date>` added (`src/main/frontend/api/http.ts`). The server then serves the records with that date standing in for the sheet's today (`LoadOrCreateSheetForRead.java`, `Sheet.previewedOn`).
- **Working out the figures:** the people and claims exports re-read their data when the button is pressed, and calculate dues on `figureToday(info.today)`, which is the preview date while one is set. So the test's Ada example comes out as expected: 10.00 normally, 11.00 with a 2026-05-01 preview, and 10.00 again once the preview is cleared.

The only edit I made is a comment line in `features/people/export.slot.tsx` and in `features/claims/export.slot.tsx` noting that exports use the preview figures. I didn't re-run the tests after adding them, since comments can't change how the app behaves.
